New driver owns prepare(). It reads the pinned candidate, baseline binding, binary, frozen primary preflight and existing packet, and writes exclusively beneath the new root. It does not call the old helpers preparation functions that execute fixture commands or change old checkouts. Candidate Git object and baseline checks are read-only. Current prepared inputs were independently checked rather than assuming source count alone proves completeness.

Selected shared launch validates binary hash, source binding and build commit; initializes a fresh explicit private base with config-only, renders runtime configuration, logs in an isolated operator and starts the owned proxy/server with explicit base and port. It does not target primary stores. The proxy is loopback-bound and forwards credentials in memory; it retains private raw payloads and responses, not request headers.

Selected aggregate apply_prompts calls the authenticated isolated /api/v1/prompts set endpoint for the two candidate sections and checks effective values. It uses fresh private client/server records; it does not edit baseline source or replace a binary. Its full checked_health call is after the sets, so this function alone is not a pre-write proof of every endpoint identity. Parent separately reports checking owned binary/base/instance health before applying them; that report is not independently re-observed here.

Selected provenance checked_health validates private effective base/masc root, expected source/binary identity, admitted singleton Flash verifier lane, no CLI/cascade/degradation, and both effective prompt sections. submit() calls it before its Goal operations.

submit() creates submission-private with exist_ok=False, verifies and copies only staged rows under private runtime playground, then uses its private Client. There is exactly one create/upsert call, one measurement call and one request_complete call. Client requests have no retry loop. A second whole-submit invocation cannot pass the exclusive output-directory creation. This is not a guarantee against asynchronous provider or outbox retry behavior, which must be read from actual evidence.

No verdict is forced, and no explicit evidence references or instruction to approve are injected by submit(). The expected_outcome diagnostic is saved locally, not passed as a model verdict or API gate.
